per_frame.summary: This is the **GitHub login page**, featuring fields for username/email and password, a green "Sign in" button, options to continue with Google or Apple, and links to create an account or sign in with a passkey.
The **Username or email address** input field became focused (active), as indicated by the blue highlight/border appearing around it in the second screenshot.
The username field changed from being empty (with a blue focus border) to containing the text "zhizhongs" (with a standard border).
The username field changed from **"zhizhongs"** to **"zhizhongs@uchicago.edu"**, indicating the user updated their login credential from a username to a full email address.
The password field became focused (highlighted with a blue border) in the second screenshot, indicating the user clicked on it.
A password was entered in the password field (shown as masked dots) between the two screenshots.
The password field lost focus (was deselected) between the two screenshots, as indicated by the blue highlight border disappearing and the cursor no longer being visible in the field.

The user successfully entered their credentials (email: zhizhongs@uchicago.edu and password) and clicked "Sign in," which navigated them from the GitHub login page to the two-factor authentication page, where they are now prompted to approve a sign-in request via the GitHub Mobile app.
The sign-in request timed out, resulting in a error banner ("Sign-in request timed out. We could not verify your identity") appearing and a green "Retry GitHub Mobile" button being added to the page.
The sign-in request timed out error was dismissed and the "More options" menu was expanded, revealing the **Authenticator app** and **2FA recovery code** alternative authentication methods.

The GitHub two-factor authentication page switched from the **GitHub Mobile app approval** method (first screen) to the **Authenticator app** method (second screen), now displaying a code entry field and a "Verify" button after the user clicked "Authenticator app."
The user successfully completed GitHub's two-factor authentication and was redirected to their GitHub Dashboard homepage.
